components.title: I'm ready to get knitting ... how about you?

components.html:
Let's take a look at 2x2 ribbing (and other needle arrangements). Many knitters get frustrated with the cast on method presented in our manuals. There are many steps for a beautiful cast on, easy to forget, but the results are sooo worth it!
Yes, you could work a the "Easiest, Best ribber Cast on". (Cast on over all needles on the main bed, then transfer stitches to the ribber in any arrangement).
But that's not why we're here ... you want to master your ribber? Master this technique.
This 2x2 Ribbing Cast on is also known as 2x2 Full Pitch Rib.
Notice the position of the needles in relation to each bed. 2 needles in work, 2 out of work on each bed.

slides.caption:
Engage Ribber and put needles into work
Needles in WORKING POSITION (Not all the way out)
  1. Pitch P
  2. Rack 5
  3. End needles on the main bed

Set up for Cast on
  1. Pitch H
  2. Rack to 4
  3. Push single needle on ribber into work

Adjust Tension for Cast on Edge
  1. Tighten tension on both carriages as tight as possible for your yarn
    Brother Knitters: move Slide lever to II (2 for Tiny)

Knit Zig-Zag Row
  1. Maintain settings (Pitch H | Rack 4)
  2. Knit 1 row right to left - Both beds should knit and a zig-zag should form.
(That extra needle on the left will help cast on the left 2 stitches. It will be removed when the cast on is done)

Insert Cast on Comb
  1. Carefully ensure the loops are engaged
  2. Be sure to include the loop of the working yarn
  3. TIP: Mark the center of the comb with color, so the comb is centered in the work and the weights hang evenly
  4. Hang some weight appropriate for your yarn and width of knitting
Does your zig-zag row look like this? If not, start over and follow each step exactly.

Some machines have separate buttons to slip from right to left, others do not. Check your manual and practice slipping in one direction before starting.
    Knit First Circular Row
    (1 of 3)
  1. Carriage is on the LEFT
  2. Set Main Bed to knit to the right
    AND
    Set Ribber to slip
  3. Knit 1 row from left to right ON THE MAIN BED ONLY

Knit Second Circular Row
    (2 of 3))
  1. Carriage is on the RIGHT
  2. Set Main Bed to knit to slip
    AND
    Set Ribber to knit to the LEFT
  3. Knit 1 row from right to left ON THE RIBBER BED ONLY

Knit Last Circular Row
    (3 of 3)
  1. Carriage is on the LEFT
  2. Set Main Bed to knit to the right
    AND
    Set Ribber to slip
  3. Knit 1 row from left to right ON THE MAIN BED ONLY
You will have knit 2 rows on the main bed and 1 row on the ribber. Note that the yarn isn't traveling between the beds at this point.

1. Transfer the single stitch from the ribber to the main bed
  2. Put the emptied needle into out of work position

Adjust to Garment Tension
  1. Set the carriage tensions to your garment tensions
  2. Brother Knitters - set slide lever to I

Set carriage to Knitting Position (Pitch P - Rack 5)
  1. Knit the ribbing for your desired length
Notice that both beds are knitting and the yarn is zig-zagging between the beds.

This zig zag row has a problem ....
  • Can you see what's wrong?
  • What needs to be changed?

The right side isn't right ...
  • The cast on comb can't be hung

AH HA!
The needles sequence on the ribber is not correct!
Gotta start over .....
Forget to raise that extra needle on the ribber?  You'll know immediately when you try to hang the cast on comb.
Not to worry!  Just pick up the loop between the 2 main bed stitches and pick up the single needle on the ribber.  Now you'll be able to secure those stitches with the cast on comb.

Changing colors or adding a new yarn?
Use a double-eye needle to drop the tail between the beds.

components.html: Compare the 2 needle arrangements

1. Engage ribber
    • Pitch "H" (half pitch)
    • Rack 5
  2. Select needles as shown: (note there are 2 needles on the main bed on each edge)
  3. Run the carriages without yarn to align the needles to working position
  4. Swing the ribber to the right 1 number (4)
  5. Bring up one needle on the ribber to working position
  6. Tighten the tension on both beds
  7. Knit a Zig Zag row
  8. Hang cast on comb and weights
  9. Knit 3 rows of tubular knitting
  10. Rack back to the left (5)
  11. Transfer the added ribber stitch on the left to the main bed
    Cast on Complete - Start Knitting
  12. Set tension on both carriages to garment tension
  13. Set row counter to 000
  14. Set both carriages to plain knitting
Compare this sample to your 2x2 sample.

slides.caption: When you remove the cast on comb, the edge is flared and a bit distorted.
Insert a blocking wire (or the wire from the cast on comb) in each of the loops across the edges and steam. Then block your ribbing as desired.

This beautiful "tubular" edge is the end result.
Notice that this is the "right" or public side of the cast on. It is the edge that had only 1 slipped row.

This is the "wrong" or private side of the cast on. It is the edge that had 2 slipped rows.
How would you control which side is which?
(Hint: It has to do with where the carriage starts for the initial zig-zag row. Pay attention when making your samples)
Examine your samples to identify the right and wrong side of the cast on edge.

components.html:
When working on the double bed, there are many alternate ways of casting on and crafting beautiful hems.
The Knit it Now eBook, Machine Knit Trims and Edges - Double Bed Edition. will Inspire you to make the edges of your ribbing a focal point of your knitting.
Now that you are getting more comfortable with your ribber, these trims and edges will be a piece of cake for you!

In the first part of this knit-along, we used the racking handle to position the ribber needles. But you may have just been following instructions and not understood exactly why we were racking.

Don't skip this section

It is critical that you understand the mechanics of racking on YOUR machine, so you can explore the technique to it's fullest. You will use racking for interesting hems and all-over fabric creation.

components.title: Down to the basics with Flat Rib

components.html:
This stitch pattern combines needles out of work and exaggerated racking. You will be racking (swinging) the ribber from the far left to the far right and back again.
Please give this one a try ... you will be inspired to try different needle arrangements and racking sequences.

Many interesting ribber stitch patterns instruct you to "Tuck Left" or "Tuck Right". It is critical that you know and UNDERSTAND the settings for your machine. (Without having to pull out your manual every time)
If you haven't already, make yourself a cheat sheet by working the following steps.
Tuck on the MAIN BED: Cast on for 1x1 ribbing (with any method) and knit a few rows. End with the carriage on the RIGHT.
  • Set the main bed carriage to tuck in BOTH Directions
  • Knit left (main bed needles should tuck)
  • Knit right (main bed needles should tuck again)
  • There should be 2 tucked stitches on the main bed - ribber knits plain
What button(s) or lever(s) do you need to use? Knit a few rows plain. End with the carriage on the RIGHT
  • Set the main bed carriage to tuck LEFT
  • Knit left (main bed needles should tuck)
  • Knit right (main bed needles should knit)
- Ribber needles knit plain
What button(s) or lever(s) do you need to use? Knit a few rows plain. End with the carriage on the RIGHT
  • Set the main bed carriage to tuck RIGHT
  • Knit left (main bed needles should Knit)
  • Knit right (main bed needles should tuck)
- Ribber needles knit plain
What button(s) or lever(s) do you need to use?
Tuck on the RIBBER:
  • Set the ribber carriage to tuck in BOTH Directions
  • Knit left (ribber needles should tuck)
  • Knit right (ribber needles should tuck again)
  • There should be 2 tucked stitches on the ribber - main bed knits plain
What button(s) or lever(s) do you need to use? Knit a few rows plain. End with the carriage on the RIGHT
  • Set the ribber carriage to tuck LEFT
  • Knit left (ribber needles should tuck)
  • Knit right (ribber needles should knit)
What button(s) or lever(s) do you need to use? Knit a few rows plain. End with the carriage on the RIGHT
  • Set the ribber carriage to tuck RIGHT
  • Knit left (ribber needles should Knit)
  • Knit right (ribber needles should tuck)
What button(s) or lever(s) do you need to use?

Now that you are understanding the settings for your machine, there are an almost unlimited number of stitch variations that can be worked with just the machine settings.
Combine needles out of work with slip and tuck ... add racking ... the sky's the limit!
Your manual probably has a few options for some interesting stitch patterns, but take time to explore the ribber manuals for other machines. (you can download them for free here)
You should be able to translate the terminology from the different brands to your machine. Tuck is tuck, no matter what button or levers you need to set.
Pitch and Half pitch refer to the position of the needles, no matter what numbers or settings you need to make.
Get inspired and put your understanding of YOUR machine to work.
Here's a beautiful stitch pattern to get you started
Can you:
  • Set your machine for 2x2 ribbing with a needle out of work?
  • Tuck in one direction?
  • Rack?

Just because we're knitting on the double bed, doesn't mean that we have to knit rectangles!
Remember when you first started shaping on the single bed? It probably took a while to figure out what techniques worked best in each situation.
As you are shaping along the edge of your knitting, there are things to consider:
  • The position of the edge needles in relation to the needle arrangement
  • The edge needle positions when racking
  • The stitch pattern setup - plain, slip, tuck etc

Let's take this step by step, think it through AND PRACTICE shaping in double bed knitting.
NOTE: In the following exercises you will be practicing decreases and increases. Because we are all using different machines (standard, mid-gauge, bulky) the instructions are not written in stone.
We'll give instructions, but the goal is for you to UNDERSTAND the technique being practiced. Struggling with binding off? Bind off more stitches. Feeling clumsy with increasing or decreasing? Work more stitches than instructed. In other words, your sample doesn't have to match mine. Do what it takes to master the technique, even if that means dropping the work from the machine and starting again.
If you're swatch comes our perfectly .. congrats! Please share and encourage others.
If not, try again!
Now is the time to gain confidence with these techniques, not when you are working on a garment under deadline.

Increases and Decreases in 1x1 ribbing

Shaping while working 1x1 ribbing (or any needle arrangment) doensn't have to be intimidating. Keep in mind that you are working with a set number of stitches. It doesn't matter that they are arranged between 2 needlebeds.
The secret to is focus on your goal or reducing or increasing the number of stitches in work. The rest is just the confidence you'll gain with the following exercises.

components.html:
Follow along with the video and try these techniques.

START HERE (A)
  • Cast on 40(80) stitches with any method
  • End needles in work on the main bed
  • Knit in 1x1 ribbing for 2-3”
  • End with the carriage on the right

sections.title:
DECREASE More than one Stitch (B)
"Bind off 4 stitches at the beginning of the next 2 rows"
sections.bodyHtml:
1. Transfer 2 ribber stitches to the opposite empty needles on the main bed
  2. Take the ribber needles out of work. (oops ... don’t forget this)
  3. Bind off 4 stitches on the main bed. Securing the last loop on the new end needle
  4. Hang a wire weight hanger and add a small weight
  5. Knit across the row (make sure that end needle knits properly)
  6. Carriage on the left: Bind off 4 stitches on the left
  7. Knit a few rows - end with the carriage on the right

sections.title:
Simple Edge DECREASE (C)
"Decrease 1 stitch each side, every other row 4 times"
sections.bodyHtml:
Transfer stitches between the beds to reduce the number of stitches in work
  1. If the edge stitch is on the ribber, transfer it to the main bed. (Double up the main bed needle)
  2. If the edge stitch is on the mian bed, transfer it to the ribber (Double up the ribber needle)
Repeat the decreases as directed

sections.title:
INCREASE more than 1 stitch on the edge (D)
"Cast on 4 stitches at the beginning of the next 2 rows"
sections.bodyHtml:
1. Maintaining the 1x1 needle arrangement, on the carriage side, put 4 new needles into work.
  2. Zig Zag the working yarn between the 2 beds across the new needles
  3. Hang a wire weight hanger and a small weight
  4. Knit across
  5. Repeat on the opposite side
  6. Knit 2 rows

sections.title:
Simple Edge INCREASE (E)
"Increase 1 stitch each side, every other row 4 times"
sections.bodyHtml:
Work increases OPPOSITE the Carriage keeping the 1x1 needle arrangement.
  1. If the edge stitch is on the main bed, opposite the carriage pull 1 ribber needle into work
  2. Knit across
  3. Hang a wire weight hanger and small weight
  4. Opposite the carriage, maintaining the 1x1 arrangement, pull 1 needle into work.
  5. Knit across
  6. Hang a wire weight hanger and a small weight
  7. Knit back

components.html:
FINISH HERE (F)
If you are happy with the results of your exercises, finish your swatch by knitting a few rows and binding off. (Practice a 1x1 bind off method)
If you feel you need more practice, continue on this swatch until you can work 1x1 increases and decreases in your sleep!

The techniques used to shape in full needle rib are similar to those used for plain knitting (stockinette).
Keep in mind that shaping happens on both beds
Work the exercises to get comfortable with knitting garments in full needle rib.

components.html:
Follow along with the video and try these techniques.

START HERE (A)
  • Cast on 40(80) stitches with any method
  • End needles in work on the main bed
  • Knit in 1x1 ribbing for 2-3”
  • End with the carriage on the right
DECREASE More than one Stitch (B)
"Bind off 4 stitches at the beginning of the next 2 rows"
  1. Transfer 4 ribber stitches to the opposite needles on the main bed (Double up the stitches)
  2. Take the ribber needles out of work. (oops ... don’t forget this)
  3. Bind off 4 stitches on the main bed (work the doubled up stitches as a single stitch). Securing the last loop on the new end needle
  4. Hang a wire weight hanger and add a small weight
  5. Knit across the row (make sure that end needle knits properly)
  6. Carriage on the left: Bind off 4 stitches on the left
  7. Knit a few rows - end with the carriage on the right

Simple Edge DECREASE (C)
"Decrease 1 stitch each side, every other row 4 times"

Transfer stitches between the beds to reduce the number of stitches in work
  1. Decrease 1 stitch on the right
    1. Transfer 1 main bed stitch to it's neighbor
    2. Transfer 1 ribber stitch to it's neighbor
  2. Decrease 1 stitch on the left
    1. Transfer 1 main bed stitch to it's neighbor
    2. Transfer 1 ribber stitch to it's neighbor
      3. Knit 2 rows and repeat a few times

    Full Fashion DECREASE (C)
    "Decrease1 stitch each side, every other row 4 times"
    Instead of transferring the edge stitches, Transfer 2 or more stitches from the edge to decrease
    Decrease 1 stitch on the right
    • Transfer 1 main bed edge stitch to it’s neighbor
    • Transfer 1 ribber stitch to it’s neighbor

    Decrease 1 stitch on the left
    • Transfer 1 main bed edge stitch to it’s neighbor
    • Transfer 1 ribber stitch to it’s neighbor

    INCREASE more than 1 stitch on the edge (D)
    "Cast on 4 stitches at the beginning of the next 2 rows"
    Maintaining the Full Needle Rib arrangement, on the carriage side:
    1. Put 4 new MAIN BED needles into work.
    2. Put 4 new RIBBER BED needles into work.
    3. Open the latches
    4. Zig Zag the working yarn between the 2 beds across the new needles
    5. Hang a wire weight hanger and a small weight
    6. Knit across
    7. Repeat on the opposite side
    8. Knit 2 rows

    Automatic Edge INCREASE (E)
    "Increase 2 stitches every 4th row"
    NOTE: It takes 4 rows to increase 1 stitch on each edge
    Work increases OPPOSITE the Carriage keeping the full needle rib arrangement
    1. Opposite the carriage, pull 1 MAIN BED needle to work
    2. Knit across
    3. Opposite the carriage, pull 1 MAIN BED needle to work
    4. Knit across
    5. Opposite the carriage, pull 1 RIBBER needle to work
    6. Knit across
    7. Opposite the carriage, pull 1 RIBBER needle to work
    8. Knit across
    9. Hang a wire weight hanger and small weight
    10. Continue Knitting
    11. Repeat this increase sequence 2-3 more times
    You will have increased 2 GARMENT stitches over 4 rows (1 stitch on the main bed, 1 stitch on the ribber)
    Full Fashion INCREASE (E)
    "Increase 2 stitches every other row"
    Work right and left increases on the same row
    1. On the right side of the knitting, transfer 2 or more needles to the right, emptying a needle
    2. Fill the empty needle with the purl bump from the row below
    3. Repeat on the left side
    4. Knit across
    5. Hang a wire weight hanger and small weight
    6. Continue Knitting

    FINISH HERE (F)
    If you are happy with the results of your exercises, finish your swatch by knitting a few rows and binding off. (Practice a full needle rib bind off method)
    If you feel you need more practice, continue on this swatch until you can work full needle rib increases and decreases in your sleep!

There are so many variations in the techniques used to work short rows on the double bed. Your needle arrangement, racking, patterning all determine the technique you use.
But it's not hard. Start with a basic 1x1 needle arrangement and examine the wraps (remember we don't want short row holes). The move to full needle rib and again explore the steps for shaping.
Armed with this knowledge, you'll be able to determine the steps needed to short row in any needle arrangement or pattern.

When would you use short row decreases?
Single or double bed, the advantage is a smoother edge.
Let's say you want to shape a shoulder and you are instructed:
Bind off 5 stitches every other row, 5 times
Binding off would produce stairsteps that would be hard to seam.
Using short row shaping keeps the stitches on the needles, so when the shaping is done, you can scrap off, then neatly join the front and back shoulder.
Short row decreases can also be used to shape necklines, form bust darts or other garment shaping. Any time you are decreasing over every other row, you can use short row shaping.

When would you use short row increase?
Like short row decreases, using "partial knitting" offers a smoother edge than casting on stitches.
Lets say your instruction tell you to:
Increase 5 stitches every other row 5 times
Casting on multiple stitches on the edge of your knitting can produce stairsteps. By using short rows, all the stitches are on the needlebed and you'll use "partial knitting" to create the shape.
This sideways knit cardigan is a good example. To form the V neck, cast on the full width of the front ("E"), then work short row increases (instead of casting on stitches) to shape the neck. You'll have a nice smooth cast on edge (or live stitches).

sections.title:
Short Row Decreases
“Decrease 5 stitches every other row 4 times”
sections.bodyHtml:
Cast on 25 stitches in 1x1 needle setup (practice a new-to-you cast on method)
  1. Knit 10 rows
  2. Carriage on the right, set both carriages to hold both ways
  3. Opposite the carriage, put 5 needles in hold
  4. Knit across and wrap
  5. Knit back
  6. Repeat 3 more times
  7. Cancel hold and knit 1 row across all the needles - Carriage on the left Don’t bind off

sections.title:
Short Row Increases
“Increase 5 stitches every other row 4 times”
sections.bodyHtml:
25 stitches are in work in 1x1 needle setup
  1. Put all needles in hold except for 5 needles next to the carriage
  2. Optional: Break the original color and thread up a contrasting color
  3. Carriage set to hold
  4. Knit across the 5 needles in work
  5. Wrap and Knit back (carriage on the left)
  6. Put 5 more needles into working position
  7. Knit, wrap, knit
  8. Repeat 2 more times
  9. Knit 10 rows and drop the work (or practice a bind off)

This exercise is a great way to practice partial knitting with double bed needle arrangements and practice joining shoulders on the machine.
